motivation: In 2009 Miyasaka first used organometal halide perovskites as light absorbers in photovoltaic cells. In 2012 Park and Snaith independently showed that solid-state perovskite devices are efficient, and Snaith found that the material carries charge over long distances and works without a mesoporous scaffold. This opened a new class of solution-processed semiconductors. Their sharp optical absorption edge, tolerance to defects and long carrier diffusion lengths have changed what we understand about how a low-temperature-processed, polycrystalline thin film can behave. In just over a decade, power conversion efficiency rose from 3.8% to above 26%, and perovskite–silicon tandems now pass 33%. That is a pace unprecedented in photovoltaics. Commercial tandem modules are now entering the market. The discovery joins fundamental semiconductor physics to cheap renewable electricity, which is the kind of benefit to humankind that Nobel's will asks for.
